9 Executive Summar!::J 
The UNDAF was prepared throughout 2010, based on the '2010 Situalion Analysis: Key Development 
Challenges Facing Egypl' which remains valid to a great extent. A first draft of the UNDAF was finalízed 
in the beginning of 2011. The revolution of 2011 led to a postponement of the signature of the UNDAF 
to ensure that emerging issues, opportunilies and pñorities were reflected in the future wor1<. of the UN 
in Egypt. Therefore, In 2011 and 2012, the UN in close collaboralion with the Govemment of Egypt and 
its national and internalional development partners reviewed the draft UNDAF ensuñng the integration 
of these pñorities. The UNCT and Government have agreed on the following UNDAF prtoñty areas: 
Poverty Alleviation through Pro-Poor Growth and Equity; 
• Ouality Basic Services; 
• Democratic Governance: 
Food Secuñty and Nutrition; and 
• Environmental Sustainability and Natural Resource Managemenl 
A total of 24 UNDAF outcomes indicate the specific results expected in terms of institutional 
performance or human behaviour for individual and social change. Gender mainstreaming, as a cross 
sectoral responsibility. is the overarching strategy of the UNCT for making women·s and men·s 
concerns an integral dimension of the design, implementation, monitortng and evaluation of policies 
and programmes in ali UNDAF priority areas so that women and men benefit equally and inequality is 
not perpetuated. Each outcome is aocompanied by a limtted number of performance indicators to guide 
programme design and lacilitate monitoñng and evaluation after implementation. 
UNDAF implementation and coordination arrangements will be carried out by teams with clearly 
outlined responsibilities. An UNDAF Steering Committee will provide overall guidance for UNDAF 
implementation. meeting once a year on the basis of an annual report. The UNCT will be responsible 
of for the management of the UNDAF. overseeing the work of the UNDAF Priority WOfking Groups 
(PWGs), reviewing an annual work plan and the annual report. The PWGs will prepare the annual wor1<. 
plan and resulls-oriented annual report, and keep abreast of developments within their wor1<. areas. 
They will be supported by the M&E Taskforce which provides technical advice to the PWGs and UNCT 
in monitoring and reporting on UNDAF outcomes and results, and building on national M&E systems 
and mechanisms. 
The UNDAF will be systematically monitored on basis of the UNDAF Resutts Malrix that consists of a 
set of performance indicatOfS for each outcome with corresponding baselines. targets and means of 
verification. To the extent possible, the monitoring data will come from national M&E systems and data 
repositories to ensure alignment with national M&E processes, reduce transaction costs, and enhance 
national ownership and mutual accountability. 
A final evaluation oflhe UNDAF will be undertaken in the first quarter of 2017, anda Mid-Term Review 
is projected to take place towards the beginning of 2015. These exercises will assess the relevance, 
effíciency, effectiveness and sustainability of the UN system's technical and development assistance to 
Egypt, and the collective UN system's conllibutions to national pñorities. They will identify key 
achievements, lessons learned, best practices which will be factored into the design of the next 
UNDAF, 
The UNDAF foresees a total budget of 736 million US dollar for the peñod of the UNDAF. While 
considerable efforts will be required by Government and the UN to mobilize funds to carry out activities 
in line with UNDAF outcomes, this budget figure is realistic as il is in line with expenditures reported by 
UN agencies in Egypt for 2010.

Overview of the Development Setting in Egypt 
For the first time in üs history, the Arab Republic of Egypt is governed, since 1 July 2012, by a 
democratically elected civilian presiden!. This importan! achievement comes as a result of prolongad 
struggle for democracy that was at its highest lntensity during the period from January 25 to February 
11 2011 when determinad activists took to the streets or Cairo and olher major cilies. The 2011 
revolution was ruelled by a widespread sense or political, economic and social exclusion (especially 
among youlh). 
Nevertheless, Egypt has seen progress in its development agenda in recent decades. To highlight a 
rew examples: average perca pita income has increased significanlly, child and maternal mortality have 
dropped considerably, and the coverage of basic utilities- such as sale drinking water and eleclricity -
now reaches a high percentage or the population. Wlthin lhe framework or Soulh-South Cooperation 
(SSC), Egypt is also increasingly becoming a development provider. Al the same time, ü is wídely 
recognized that further progress is required on the country's human development and human lights' 
agenda. Challenges include ensuring that economic growth translates lnto improved equlty and 
poverty reduction; generating decent work opportunities, especially for youth and women; improving 
the quality of essential services (including health and education); accelerating progress on gender 
equality and women's empowerment , political participation, transparency and public accountability; 
addressing the country's high population growth rata; reducing pressure on natural resources; 
advancing on persisten! heatth challenges such as Hepatitis C. HIV/AIDS, TB and non-communicable 
15 diseases; upgrading the perfonnance of institutions; strengthening accountability, respect for human 
rights and combating corruption, 
Oue to the politícal and social unrest which followed the revolution, Egypt's economy has suffered 
considerably since 2011 resulting in a drastic impact on tha tourism sector, a decrease in foreign 
investrnents and shrinking of foreign reserves. This impact on the economy has aggravated the already 
axisting imbalances and resultad in for example higher unamployment, aspecially amongst the young 
ganeration which togethar with the low participation of women in the labour market ramains a major 
concern. In chapter 2a more detailed analysis is provided for each of the five priority areas. 
Tracking progress towards the MDGs 
The MOGs provide a good overview on the main development challenges of Egypt. Tracking Egypt's 
progress In achieving the MOGs was systematicalty carried out, through the preparation of national 
reports that were published in 2002, 2004, 2005, 2008 and 2010, These reports portray Egypt's 
progress in achieving each of the MOGs and their trend since 2000 and highlighted as well factors 
boosting andlor inhibiting progress. These reports helped provide guidance concerning the process of 
identifying priorities as well as future actions to ensure the achievement of the MOGs within target date. 
The 2010 MOG's report indicates that Egypt remains on track to achieve most of the MOGs, but also 
highlights the significan! gaps in income levels and living standards between different parts of Egypt 
and across the different segments of Egyptian society. The MOG report highlights that the most critica! 
areas of deficit are poverty and hunger, unemployment, gender disparities, and access to improved 
sanitation facilities. 11 argues that Egypt's most challenging task over the next five years is to reduce the 
incidence of those living below the national poverty line• . Unemployment is a critica! challenge. 
especially amongst youth under tha age of 30. lntansified efforts are needed to reach full and
